descripcion: At B2 the goal is to recognise and produce two clear registers — informal (contractions, phrasal verbs) and formal (no contractions, more Latinate vocabulary) — without mixing them in the same message. The finer six-axis control and full rewriting across three registers (C1) isn't the target yet.

filas: do not, it is, we are

ejemplos.texto: I regret that I am unable to attend this evening.

notas: Contractions are the fastest signal of informal register — removing them alone shifts a sentence towards formal.
Phrasal verbs (find out, sort out) are informal; their Latinate equivalents (discover, resolve) are formal.
Mixing registers within the same message — a contraction next to a very formal word — is the most common register error at this level.

es.en: Spanish marks formality mainly through tú/usted and verb forms, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary and contractions, so Spanish speakers who are polite with usted may still mix registers in English.
es.es: El español marca la formalidad principalmente mediante «tú/usted» y las formas verbales, algo que el inglés no tiene. En inglés, el registro se expresa mediante el vocabulario y las contracciones, por lo que alguien que usa correctamente «usted» puede aun así mezclar registros en inglés.

de.en: German marks formality with Sie, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?, so these need conscious attention.
de.de: Deutsch markiert Höflichkeit mit «Sie», was dem Englischen fehlt. Im Englischen wird Register über Wortschatz, Kontraktionen und Formen wie «Could you…?» gegenüber «Can you…?» ausgedrückt; darauf muss man bewusst achten.

it.en: Italian marks formality with Lei, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.
it.it: L'italiano marca la formalità con «Lei», cosa che l'inglese non fa. In inglese il registro passa attraverso lessico, contrazioni e forme come «Could you…?» rispetto a «Can you…?».

fr.en: French marks formality with vous, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.
fr.fr: Le français marque la formalité avec «vous», ce que l'anglais n'a pas. En anglais, le registre passe par le vocabulaire, les contractions et des formes comme «Could you…?» par opposition à «Can you…?».

pt.en: Portuguese marks formality with você or o senhor, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.
pt.pt: O português marca formalidade com «você» ou «o senhor/a senhora», o que o inglês não possui. Em inglês, o registro é expresso pelo vocabulário, pelas contrações e por formas como «Could you…?» em contraste com «Can you…?».

errores: Mixing a contraction with a very formal word in the same sentence.
Using a phrasal verb in a formal email where its Latinate equivalent would fit better.
Assuming formal English is just longer or harder, rather than a different set of choices.

es: *Estimado señor* rendered as *Esteemed Sir* instead of *Dear Mr …*.
de: *Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren* rendered as *Very honoured ladies and gentlemen* instead of *Dear Sir or Madam*.
it: *Gentile Signor Rossi* rendered as *Gentle Mr Rossi* instead of *Dear Mr Rossi*.
fr: The long closing *Veuillez agréer…* carried over instead of a simple *Yours sincerely* or *Kind regards*.
pt: *Exmo. Senhor* rendered as *Excellent Sir* instead of *Dear Sir*.

mision.consigna: Tell a friend and your IT department about the same data problem with a work app.
requisitos: one informal message with contractions and phrasal verbs

microtareas.texto: Write *Can't make it — sorry!* in formal register.
Rewrite a short formal email you received as a text to a friend.
Record 90 seconds explaining *artificial intelligence* to a friend, then 30 seconds formally.

autochequeo: Are contractions used consistently, either all present or all absent?
Are phrasal verbs replaced with formal equivalents in the formal version?
Is the register consistent throughout, without mixing?
Would the intended reader find the register appropriate?
Have I written the same content in both registers to compare?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on register. Check for mixed formal and informal features in the same message, especially contractions next to formal vocabulary. Do not rewrite the text.
